title: अष्टाशीतितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 88 · Eighth day: Duryodhana and the demon

summary.en: Duryodhana withstands Ghatotkacha's arrows, and the Kaurava elephants and kings charge the demon. Bhishma tells his warriors to rescue Duryodhana, and Ghatotkacha's arrows fly thick at the prince Brihadbala.
summary.kn: ದುರ್ಯೋಧನ ಘಟೋತ್ಕಚನ ಬಾಣಗಳನ್ನು ತಡೆಯುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಕೌರವ ಆನೆಗಳು, ರಾಜರು ರಾಕ್ಷಸನ ಮೇಲೆ ಎರಗುತ್ತಾರೆ. ದುರ್ಯೋಧನನನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸಲು ಭೀಷ್ಮ ಆದೇಶಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಘಟೋತ್ಕಚ ರಾಜಕುಮಾರ ಬೃಹದ್ಬಲನನ್ನು ಗಾಯಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: दुर्योधन घटोत्कच के बाणों को सहता है, और कौरव हाथी तथा राजा राक्षस पर चढ़ते हैं। भीष्म योद्धाओं को दुर्योधन की रक्षा का आदेश देते हैं, और घटोत्कच बृहद्बल को घायल करता है।
summary.te: దుర్యోధనుడు ఘటోత్కచుని బాణాలను తట్టుకుంటాడు; కౌరవ ఏనుగులు, రాజులు రాక్షసునిపై దాడి చేస్తారు. దుర్యోధనుని కాపాడమని భీష్ముడు ఆదేశిస్తాడు; ఘటోత్కచుడు బృహద్బలుని గాయపరుస్తాడు.
summary.ta: துரியோதனன் கடோத்கசனின் அம்புகளைத் தாங்குகிறான்; கௌரவ யானைகளும் மன்னர்களும் அரக்கன் மீது பாய்கின்றனர். துரியோதனனைக் காக்கும்படி பீஷ்மர் ஆணையிட, கடோத்கசன் பிருகத்பலனைக் காயப்படுத்துகிறான்.
summary.ml: ഘടോൽക്കചന്റെ അമ്പുകളെ ദുര്യോധനൻ ചെറുക്കുന്നു; കൗരവ ആനകളും രാജാക്കന്മാരും രാക്ഷസനെതിരെ ചാർജ് ചെയ്യുന്നു. ദുര്യോധനനെ രക്ഷിക്കാൻ ഭീഷ്മർ യോദ്ധാക്കളോട് കൽപ്പിക്കുന്നു; ബൃഹദ്ബലനു നേരെ ഘടോൽക്കചന്റെ അമ്പുകൾ നിറയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.88; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
ततस्तद्बाणवर्षं तु दुःसहं दानवैरपि ।
दधार युधि राजेन्द्रो यथा वर्षं महाद्विपः ॥

meaning.en: That shower of arrows, which even the danavas could not bear, the king of kings bore in the battle as a great elephant bears rain.

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टो निःश्वसन्निव पन्नगः ।
संशयं परमं प्राप्तः पुत्रस्ते भरतर्षभ ॥

meaning.en: Then, filled with anger and hissing like a snake, your son, O best of Bharatas, was in great peril.

verses.text:
मुमोच निशितांस्तीक्ष्णान्नाराचान्पञ्चविंशतिम् ।
तेऽपतन्सहसा राजंस्तस्मिन्राक्षसपुंगवे ।
आशीविषा इव क्रुद्धाः पर्वते गन्धमादने ॥

meaning.en: He loosed twenty-five sharp, keen iron arrows. They fell suddenly on that chief of rakshasas like angry venomous snakes on Mount Gandhamadana.

verses.text:
स तैर्विद्धः स्रवन्रक्तं प्रभिन्न इव कुञ्जरः ।
दध्रे मतिं विनाशाय राज्ञः स पिशिताशनः ।
जग्राह च महाशक्तिं गिरीणामपि दारणीम् ॥

meaning.en: Pierced by them and streaming blood like an elephant with its rut flowing, the flesh-eater set his mind on the king's destruction and took up a great spear that could split even mountains.

verses.text:
संप्रदीप्तां महोल्काभामशनीं मघवानिव ।
समुद्यच्छन्महाबाहुर्जिघांसुस्तनयं तव ॥

meaning.en: Blazing like a great meteor, like a thunderbolt in the hand of Indra, the long-armed one raised it, wishing to kill your son.

verses.text:
तामुद्यतामभिप्रेक्ष्य वङ्गानामधिपस्त्वरन् ।
कुञ्जरं गिरिसंकाशं राक्षसं प्रत्यचोदयत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing it raised, the king of the Vangas hurriedly drove his mountain-like elephant at the rakshasa.

verses.text:
स नागप्रवरेणाजौ बलिना शीघ्रगामिना ।
यतो दुर्योधनरथस्तं मार्गं प्रत्यपद्यत ।
रथं च वारयामास कुञ्जरेण सुतस्य ते ॥

meaning.en: On that great, strong, swift elephant he took the path where Duryodhana's chariot stood, and blocked the rakshasa with his elephant in front of your son's chariot.

verses.text:
मार्गमावारितं दृष्ट्वा राज्ञा वङ्गेन धीमता ।
घटोत्कचो महाराज क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ।
उद्यतां तां महाशक्तिं तस्मिंश्चिक्षेप वारणे ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the way blocked by the wise king of Vanga, Ghatotkacha, O great king, his eyes red with fury, hurled the great raised spear at that elephant.

verses.text:
स तयाभिहतो राजंस्तेन बाहुविमुक्तया ।
संजातरुधिरोत्पीडः पपात च ममार च ॥

meaning.en: Struck by it, thrown from his arm, O king, the elephant spouted a flood of blood and fell and died.

verses.text:
पतत्यथ गजे चापि वङ्गानामीश्वरो बली ।
जवेन समभिद्रुत्य जगाम धरणीतलम् ॥

meaning.en: As the elephant fell, the strong king of Vanga quickly leapt down and went to the ground.

verses.text:
दुर्योधनोऽपि संप्रेक्ष्य पातितं वरवारणम् ।
प्रभग्नं च बलं दृष्ट्वा जगाम परमां व्यथाम् ॥

meaning.en: Duryodhana too, seeing the great elephant brought down and his army broken, was greatly pained.

verses.text:
क्षत्रधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य आत्मनश्चाभिमानिताम् ।
प्राप्तेऽपक्रमणे राजा तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः ॥

meaning.en: Keeping the kshatriya's duty and his own pride before him, though the time for retreat had come, the king stood firm like a mountain.

verses.text:
संधाय च शितं बाणं कालाग्निसमतेजसम् ।
मुमोच परमक्रुद्धस्तस्मिन्घोरे निशाचरे ॥

meaning.en: Fitting a sharp arrow with the brilliance of the fire of doom, he loosed it in great anger at that terrible night-roamer.

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य बाणमिन्द्राशनिप्रभम् ।
लाघवाद्वञ्चयामास महाकायो घटोत्कचः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that arrow come, bright as Indra's thunderbolt, huge Ghatotkacha dodged it with his quickness.

verses.text:
भूय एव ननादोग्रः क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ।
त्रासयन्सर्वभूतानि युगान्ते जलदो यथा ॥

meaning.en: He roared again, fierce, his eyes red with rage, terrifying all beings like a cloud at the end of an age.

verses.text:
तं श्रुत्वा निनदं घोरं तस्य भीष्मस्य रक्षसः ।
आचार्यमुपसंगम्य भीष्मः शांतनवोऽब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing that terrible roar of that rakshasa, Bhishma, son of Shantanu, went to the teacher Drona and said:

verses.text:
यथैष निनदो घोरः श्रूयते राक्षसेरितः ।
हैडिम्बो युध्यते नूनं राज्ञा दुर्योधनेन ह ॥

meaning.en: From the terrible roar we hear sent up by the rakshasa, surely Hidimba's son is fighting King Duryodhana.

verses.text:
नैष शक्यो हि संग्रामे जेतुं भूतेन केनचित् ।
तत्र गच्छत भद्रं वो राजानं परिरक्षत ॥

meaning.en: No being can conquer him in battle. Go there, good fortune to you, and guard the king.

verses.text:
अभिद्रुतं महाभागं राक्षसेन दुरात्मना ।
एतद्धि परमं कृत्यं सर्वेषां नः परंतपाः ॥

meaning.en: The fortunate king is attacked by the wicked rakshasa. This is the highest duty of all of us, tormentors of foes.

verses.text:
पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा त्वरमाणा महारथाः ।
उत्तमं जवमास्थाय प्रययुर्यत्र कौरवः ॥

meaning.en: Hearing the grandfather's words, the great chariot-warriors hurried at the greatest speed to where the Kaurava was.

verses.text:
द्रोणश्च सोमदत्तश्च बाह्लिकश्च जयद्रथः ।
कृपो भूरिश्रवाः शल्यश्चित्रसेनो विविंशतिः ॥

meaning.en: Drona, Somadatta, Bahlika, Jayadratha, Kripa, Bhurishravas, Shalya, Chitrasena, Vivimshati,

verses.text:
अश्वत्थामा विकर्णश्च आवन्त्यश्च बृहद्बलः ।
रथाश्चानेकसाहस्रा ये तेषामनुयायिनः ।
अभिद्रुतं परीप्सन्तः पुत्रं दुर्योधनं तव ॥

meaning.en: Ashvatthama, Vikarna, the Avanti prince and Brihadbala, and the many thousands of chariots that followed them, went wishing to save your son Duryodhana, who was under attack.

verses.text:
तदनीकमनाधृष्यं पालितं लोकसत्तमैः ।
आततायिनमायान्तं प्रेक्ष्य राक्षससत्तमः ।
नाकम्पत महाबाहुर्मैनाक इव पर्वतः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that unassailable army, guarded by the best men in the world, coming at him with weapons raised, that best of rakshasas, long-armed, did not tremble, like Mount Mainaka.

verses.text:
प्रगृह्य विपुलं चापं ज्ञातिभिः परिवारितः ।
शूलमुद्गरहस्तैश्च नानाप्रहरणैरपि ॥

meaning.en: Taking up his huge bow, surrounded by his kinsmen with spears and clubs in their hands and many other weapons,

verses.text:
ततः समभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम् ।
राक्षसानां च मुख्यस्य दुर्योधनबलस्य च ॥

meaning.en: a tumultuous, hair-raising battle then took place between the chief of the rakshasas and Duryodhana's force.

verses.text:
धनुषां कूजतां शब्दः सर्वतस्तुमुलोऽभवत् ।
अश्रूयत महाराज वंशानां दह्यतामिव ॥

meaning.en: The sound of the twanging bows rose tumultuous on every side, and was heard, O great king, like the sound of burning bamboo.

verses.text:
शस्त्राणां पात्यमानानां कवचेषु शरीरिणाम् ।
शब्दः समभवद्राजन्नद्रीणामिव दीर्यताम् ॥

meaning.en: The sound of the weapons falling on the armor of embodied men was like the sound of cliffs splitting, O king.

verses.text:
वीरबाहुविसृष्टानां तोमराणां विशां पते ।
रूपमासीद्वियत्स्थानां सर्पाणां सर्पतामिव ॥

meaning.en: The javelins thrown from the arms of heroes looked, lord of men, like snakes crawling in the sky.

verses.text:
ततः परमसंक्रुद्धो विस्फार्य सुमहद्धनुः ।
राक्षसेन्द्रो महाबाहुर्विनदन्भैरवं रवम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the long-armed lord of rakshasas, in great fury, stretched his huge bow and roared a fearful roar.

verses.text:
आचार्यस्यार्धचन्द्रेण क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् ।
सोमदत्तस्य भल्लेन ध्वजमुन्मथ्य चानदत् ॥

meaning.en: Angry, he cut the teacher's bow with a crescent-headed arrow, and roaring, struck down Somadatta's banner with a barbed arrow.

verses.text:
बाह्लिकं च त्रिभिर्बाणैरभ्यविध्यत्स्तनान्तरे ।
कृपमेकेन विव्याध चित्रसेनं त्रिभिः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: He struck Bahlika in the chest with three arrows, Kripa with one, and Chitrasena with three arrows.

verses.text:
पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन सम्यक्प्रणिहितेन च ।
जत्रुदेशे समासाद्य विकर्णं समताडयत् ।
न्यषीदत्स रथोपस्थे शोणितेन परिप्लुतः ॥

meaning.en: With a well-aimed arrow drawn fully and loosed, he struck Vikarna at the collarbone, and Vikarna sank down on his chariot floor, drenched in blood.

verses.text:
ततः पुनरमेयात्मा नाराचान्दश पञ्च च ।
भूरिश्रवसि संक्रुद्धः प्राहिणोद्भरतर्षभ ।
ते वर्म भित्त्वा तस्याशु प्राविशन्मेदिनीतलम् ॥

meaning.en: Then that man of boundless spirit sent fifteen iron arrows at Bhurishravas in his anger, best of Bharatas, and they pierced his armor and quickly entered the ground.

verses.text:
विविंशतेश्च द्रौणेश्च यन्तारौ समताडयत् ।
तौ पेततू रथोपस्थे रश्मीनुत्सृज्य वाजिनाम् ॥

meaning.en: He struck the charioteers of Vivimshati and of Drona's son, and they fell on the chariot floors, dropping the reins of the horses.

verses.text:
सिन्धुराज्ञोऽर्धचन्द्रेण वाराहं स्वर्णभूषितम् ।
उन्ममाथ महाराज द्वितीयेनाच्छिनद्धनुः ॥

meaning.en: With a crescent-headed arrow he tore down the gold-adorned boar banner of the king of the Sindhus, and with a second he cut his bow, O great king.

verses.text:
चतुर्भिरथ नाराचैरावन्त्यस्य महात्मनः ।
जघान चतुरो वाहान्क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ॥

meaning.en: With four iron arrows, his eyes red with anger, he killed the four horses of the great-souled prince of Avanti.

verses.text:
पूर्णायतविसृष्टेन पीतेन निशितेन च ।
निर्बिभेद महाराज राजपुत्रं बृहद्बलम् ।
स गाढविद्धो व्यथितो रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् ॥

meaning.en: With a drawn, sharp arrow he pierced the prince Brihadbala, O great king, who, deeply wounded and pained, sat down on the chariot floor.

verses.text:
भृशं क्रोधेन चाविष्टो रथस्थो राक्षसाधिपः ।
चिक्षेप निशितांस्तीक्ष्णाञ्शरानाशीविषोपमान् ।
बिभिदुस्ते महाराज शल्यं युद्धविशारदम् ॥

meaning.en: Standing on his chariot, the lord of rakshasas, filled with great anger, shot sharp arrows like venomous snakes, and they pierced Shalya, skilled in battle, O great king.
